q: At the present rate of consumption, petroleum and natural gas may run out within ____ years.
e: At the present rate of consumption, petroleum and natural gas may run out within 50 years.

q: At the present rate of consumption, coal will only last for a further ____ years.
e: At the present rate of consumption, coal reserves will only last for a further 250 years.

q: An alternative fuel is an internal combustion engine fuel other than gasoline or ____ oil.
e: An alternative fuel is any internal combustion engine fuel other than gasoline or diesel oil.

q: Alternative fuels include natural gas, propane, hydrogen fuel, biomass-derived fuels, biodiesel, bio-alcohols and ____.
e: Alternative fuels include natural gas, propane, hydrogen, biodiesel, bio-alcohols, and electricity.

q: Hydrogen fuel, biomass-derived fuels, biodiesel and bio-alcohols are ____ fuels.
e: Hydrogen fuel, biodiesel, and bio-alcohols are classified as renewable fuels.

q: LPG stands for Liquefied ____ Gas.
e: LPG stands for Liquefied Petroleum Gas.

q: LPG is composed of propane and ____.
e: LPG is composed of a mixture of propane and butane.

q: CNG contains 90% ____.
e: CNG (Compressed Natural Gas) contains approximately 90% methane.

q: Biodiesel is composed of long chain ____.
e: Biodiesel consists of long-chain alkyl esters derived from plant or animal oils.

q: Biogas is produced from waste organic matter and its main composition is ____.
e: Biogas is produced from waste organic matter and its main composition is methane.

q: Gasohol is a blended fuel of petrol and ____.
e: Gasohol is a blended fuel made of petrol and ethanol.

q: A common gasohol mixture is 90% petrol and ____% ethanol.
e: A common gasohol mixture consists of 90% petrol and 10% ethanol.

q: Plant or animal oils have to be converted to biodiesel by ____.
e: Plant or animal oils are converted to biodiesel through a process called transesterification.

q: The transesterification process involves the addition of potassium hydroxide or sodium hydroxide as a basic ____.
e: Transesterification involves the addition of potassium hydroxide or sodium hydroxide as a basic catalyst.

q: The solution is heated to ____°C during the transesterification process.
e: During transesterification, the seed oil and catalytic solution are heated to 60°C.

q: The transesterification process produces methyl or ethyl ester as the product and ____.
e: The transesterification process produces methyl or ethyl ester (biodiesel) and glycerol.

q: Pure biodiesel is separated out by removing glycerine and sodium or potassium salt of fatty acids, which is also known as ____.
e: Glycerine and the sodium or potassium salt of fatty acids, known as soap, are removed by washing with water.

q: Most hydrogen is manufactured on a large scale in industry from petrol and natural ____.
e: Most hydrogen is manufactured on a large scale in industry from petrol and natural gas.

q: A mixture of methane and steam is passed over a ____ catalyst to produce carbon monoxide and hydrogen.
e: A mixture of methane and steam is passed over a nickel catalyst to produce carbon monoxide and hydrogen.

q: The carbon monoxide gas is then reacted with more steam to produce carbon dioxide and ____.
e: Carbon monoxide reacts with more steam to produce carbon dioxide and additional hydrogen.

q: The hydrogen is separated from the carbon dioxide by passing the gases through an ____ to absorb the acidic carbon dioxide.
e: Hydrogen is separated from carbon dioxide by passing the gases through an alkali to absorb the acidic CO2.

q: Smaller quantities of hydrogen are produced by the electrolysis of water containing ____ acid.
e: Smaller quantities of hydrogen are produced by the electrolysis of water containing sulphuric acid.

q: The chemical equation for the electrolysis of water is $2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2H_2(g) +$ ____.
e: The electrolysis of water produces hydrogen gas and oxygen gas, represented as $2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2H_2(g) + O_2(g)$.

q: Hydrogen burns cleanly in air, and the product is ____, which is a non-pollutant.
e: Hydrogen burns cleanly in air, and the only product is steam, which is a non-pollutant.

q: The chemical equation for hydrogen burning in air is $2H_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightarrow$ ____.
e: The chemical equation for hydrogen burning cleanly in air is $2H_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightarrow 2H_2O(g)$.

q: Hydrogen produces at least twice as much heat energy per gram when burnt, than any other common ____.
e: Hydrogen produces at least twice as much heat energy per gram when burnt than any other common fuel.

q: Methane gas is formed naturally when anaerobic bacteria help decomposition of organic matter under geological conditions to produce natural ____.
e: Anaerobic bacteria help decompose organic matter under geological conditions to produce natural gas.

q: In India and China, biomass ____ are important sources of fuel for villages.
e: In India and China, biomass digesters are important sources of fuel for villages.

q: The order for the main energy sources currently used in the world in terms of producing energy is: crude oil > coal > natural gas > hydroelectric > nuclear fission > wind > biofuels > solar > ____.
e: The order of main energy sources currently used in the world ends with solar and geothermal energy.

q: Plant oil, hydroelectric, wind, biofuels, solar and geothermal are all ____ energy sources.
e: Plant oil, hydroelectric, wind, biofuels, solar, and geothermal are all renewable energy sources.

q: Natural gas offshore projects in Myanmar are Yadana project, Yetagon project, Shwe Platform project and ____ project.
e: Natural gas offshore projects in Myanmar include Yadana, Yetagon, Shwe Platform, and Zawtika.
